title: Races and Circular Motion
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Races and Circular Motion. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Race comparisons

For the same race distance, speed is inversely proportional to finishing time. If A beats B by d metres in a race of length L, then when A finishes B has covered L-d. Their speed ratio is (L:(L-d)). Use distance = speed × time to find a missing value.

Circular tracks

On a circular track of length C, runners moving in opposite directions meet at relative speed u+v; those moving in the same direction meet at |u-v|. The first meeting time is track length divided by relative speed. Subsequent meetings occur at the same interval if speeds stay constant.

Worked example: On a 400 m track, runners move in opposite directions at 6 m/s and 4 m/s. Relative speed is 10 m/s, so they first meet after (\(400/10=40\)) seconds.

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• At the instant the winner finishes, compare the loser's covered distance with the full race length.
  • Use relative speed; add for opposite directions and subtract for the same direction.
  • For repeated meetings, count relative laps rather than individual laps.
  • Convert track length and speeds to compatible units.
  • Distinguish a meeting, an overtake and a finish gap.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• For equal race distance, speed ratio is the inverse of time ratio.
  • If A beats B by d in an L-metre race, (\(v_A/v_B=L/(L-d)\)).
  • First circular-track meeting time = circumference / relative speed.
  • Same direction: relative speed = absolute speed difference.
  • Opposite directions: relative speed = sum of speeds.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    Two runners move in opposite directions on a 400 m track at 6 m/s and 4 m/s. When do they first meet?

    1. (\(20\text{ s}\))
    2. (\(40\text{ s}\))
    3. (\(50\text{ s}\))
    4. (\(100\text{ s}\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(40\text{ s}\))

    Their relative speed is (\(6+4=10\)) m/s. Time (\(=400/10=40\)) s.

  2. Core:

    In a 100 m race, A finishes in 10 s and beats B by 20 m. How long does B take to finish 100 m at the same speed?

    1. (\(10\text{ s}\))
    2. (\(11.5\text{ s}\))
    3. (\(12.5\text{ s}\))
    4. (\(15\text{ s}\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(12.5\text{ s}\))

    When A covers 100 m, B covers 80 m in 10 s, so B's speed is 8 m/s. B's 100 m time is (\(100/8=12.5\)) s.

  3. Foundation:

    Two runners move in opposite directions on a 400 m track at 6 m/s and 4 m/s. When do they first meet?

    1. (\(20 s\))
    2. (\(30 s\))
    3. (\(40 s\))
    4. (\(50 s\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(40 s\))

    Relative speed is (\(6+4=10\)) m/s. Time is (\(400/10=40\)) seconds.

  4. Standard:

    In a 100 m race, A finishes in 10 seconds and beats B by 20 m. How long does B take to run 100 m at the same speed?

    1. (\(10 s\))
    2. (\(11 s\))
    3. (\(12.5 s\))
    4. (\(15 s\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(12.5 s\))

    When A finishes, B has run 80 m in 10 s, so B's speed is 8 m/s. Time for 100 m is (\(100/8=12.5\)) s.

  5. Challenge:

    Two runners start together on a 500 m circular track and run in the same direction at 7 m/s and 5 m/s. After how long does the faster runner first lap the slower one?

    1. (\(100 s\))
    2. (\(200 s\))
    3. (\(250 s\))
    4. (\(500 s\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(250 s\))

    Relative speed is (\(7-5=2\)) m/s. One full lap of separation requires 500 m, so time is (\(500/2=250\)) seconds.
